text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- After three days of talks between the factions it's still not clear who will be the country's finance minister. The Democratic Party Saimnieks proposed that the post be taken by its leader, Ziedonis Chevers but this was rejected by Prime Minister Andris Shkele. He wants another Saimnieks man, businessman and MP Atis Sausnitis to be finance minister.
- Parliament is expected to vote on the new government today.

- Other key ministries have already been filled with defence going to Andrejks Krastinsh, economics to Guntar Krasts and transport to Vilis Krishtopans. The new cabinet has done awy with the posts of minister of state.

- Latvian Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs rejected a Russian concept for long-term relations with the Baltic States. Birkavs said that the Russian stand with regard to Baltics is nothing of surprise. Birkavs said he sees no reason for Latvia to alter its strategy aimed at joining NATO.

- Russian Ambassador to Latvia, Alexander Udaltsov, announced that Russian Duma vice-speaker Serguey Baburin will be the official in charge of receiving Latvian delegation. The Russian Ambassador made it clear his country expects Latvia to take a reasonable stand and to respect Russia's interests.
- The commanders of the armed forces of Latvia and Czech Republic, Juris Dalbins and Jiry Niekvasil, have agreed on developing military co-operationn between the two nations.

- Since the start of the year, the lat has lost more and more to the dollar. The central bank said the dollar is rising against all currencies and interest rates are falling in Latvia, which means fewer foreigners are buying lats to take part in T-bill auctions.
- Riga district court agreed to the claim of the Bank of Latvia and ruled that the G24 credits serviced by the collapsed Banka Baltija should be given over to Parex Bank.
